HediffDef.label: gear-rot trap implant
HediffDef.description:
A chest implant that turns its host into a last weapon: when the host dies it ruptures and releases a gear-rot fume cloud.

The answer to raiders who stroll through gas lines behind sealed masks. Gear-rot ignores the wearer and eats the kit: fabric, polymer, ceramic plate and steel pit and crumble in minutes.

- In thick fume, every worn item loses 2-5% of its hit points per second.
- Masks, helmets and armor that reach zero fall apart, leaving the wearer open to whatever else is in the air.
- Uncovered skin takes acid burns.
Mix it with a lethal gas.

Lethality 3/5. Complexity 4/5. Research: corrosive agents.

HediffDef.label: scourge trap implant
HediffDef.description:
A chest implant that turns its host into a last weapon: when the host dies it ruptures and releases a scourge fog cloud.

A heavy, clinging acid for ground you never want back. Nothing worth salvaging survives where it settles, and it does not care what you are wearing.

- Kills every plant it touches: crops, grass and trees.
- Dissolves weapons, apparel, corpses and resources lying on the ground.
- Eats doors, barricades, traps, conduits and walls. Wood goes in seconds, steel in under a minute, stone and plasteel hold out far longer.
- Burns skin straight through ordinary clothes and armor. A gas mask shields only the face and lungs; a chemical suit only the body. Only both together keep it off.
- Breathed without a mask it burns the lungs. Half a minute in thick fog and the lungs fill with fluid over the next hours: fatal unless a doctor treats it. Badly burned lungs scar for good.
Raiders path around scourge fog unless sapping orders drive them through.

Lethality 2.5/5. Complexity 4/5. Research: corrosive agents.

HediffDef.label: deathbreath trap implant
HediffDef.description:
A chest implant that turns its host into a last weapon: when the host dies it ruptures and releases a deathbreath fog cloud.

Developed for trench wars on a world with nobody left to remember them. An odourless asphyxiant that shuts a body down in stages: the brain, then the lungs, then the heart.

Living creatures only; mechanoids are immune.
- About 2 seconds in dense fog: collapse.
- About 5 seconds: respiratory and cardiac arrest.
- Pawns pulled out right after collapsing live, but usually with hypoxic brain scarring or myocardial necrosis that only glitterworld surgery, a biosculpter or a healer mech serum can repair.
- After about 3 seconds the dose is lethal: deathbreath poisoning keeps spreading after the pawn is out and kills within hours unless a doctor treats it.
Breathed in: a gas mask stops it completely; toxic resistance reduces the dose.

Lethality 5/5. Complexity 2/5. Research: terminal asphyxiants.
